found_values.value: One output of the I/O expander per biased line, 5 in all: the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket. A resistor holds each control input at the pull-down selection, so the reset and unpowered state selects the pull-down (V57's condition). The expander resets with the RP2354B and its driving pin is then an input (IOBoard.md:340). A jumper cannot follow a mode firmware sets per binding (IOBoard.md:64, :230). A circuit with no control input cannot tell the modes apart: bidirectional DShot and the UART-based modes idle high, servo PWM, PPM and plain DShot idle low (IOBoard.md:251, :253, :256). An RP2354B GPIO also meets V57, because Bank 0 pads reset pulled low (section 9.3), and costs 5 GPIO. The expander's output count is V119 (R6)

found_values.value: With the pin released, the UART socket and a multiprotocol port in ESC bootloader, ESC telemetry, servo configuration or VESC mode take a switched 1 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V, in parallel with the fixed 10 kOhm pull-down: the idle is 3.3 x 10 / 11 = 3.0 V. With the gate disabled the line has the 10 kOhm pull-down alone while the selector is at its reset or unpowered state (V57); a disabled line whose pull-up firmware keeps selected idles at 3.0 V. Evidence: AM32's bootloader samples the line against its own pull-down and stays only if the line never reads low (bootloader/main.c:1097-1138) and receives with its pull-up (main.c:516). BLHeli_S's bootloader sets its pin open-drain and high ('Disable pushpull', 'Set data high', BLHeliBootLoad.inc:71-72), so its high comes from a pull-up. AM32's G071 telemetry pin is open-drain with pull-up (serial_telemetry.c, GPIO init). A Hitec D-series servo drives low only and holds a 3k pull-down; the library asks for 1 kOhm to 3.3 V on a 3.3 V controller (HitecDServoInternal.h Fundamentals; README.md:11). OpenYGE is UART 8N1 (docs/OpenYGE.md:21) and idles high. 1 kOhm against the servo's 3 kOhm and the board's 10 kOhm (2.31 kOhm together) puts the line at 3.3 x 2.31 / 3.31 = 2.30 V, above V_IH 2.0 V (Table 1436); above 1.50 kOhm it falls under 2.0 V

One signal wire, the servo's PWM line, at half duplex. UART with inverted polarity: idle low, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. The servo's output drives low only and the servo holds a 3 kOhm pull-down; the programmer supplies the pull-up. After power-up or a write to the REBOOT register the servo ignores PWM and serial for 1000 ms and drives the line low. Source status as V60

3.3 V, driven from the 3.3 V rail, on the 16 PWM ports, the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket; no supply is sensed from the device. found_values.value: 1 kOhm to 3.3 V: the switched pull-up of V58, in parallel with the fixed 10 kOhm pull-down, idle 3.0 V. The pull-up only holds the idle: the ESC drives the reply push-pull. AM32 sends it from a timer output (Mcu/g071/Src/IO.c, sendDshotDma, CCMR1 = 0x60); Bluejay sets its pin push-pull for the reply (src/Modules/Isrs.asm:481). AM32 targets pull their input up, except NEUTRONRC_G071, which pulls it down (Src/main.c:1930-1934). With the pull-up selected the RP2354B sinks (3.3 - 0.5) V / 1 kOhm = 2.8 mA while it drives low, within the 4 mA drive setting at V_OL 0.5 V (Table 1436). One value serves every mode that idles high, because Hitec servo configuration needs 1.50 kOhm or less (V58)

found_values.value: Low, on every gated line, while the RP2354B is held in reset and while it restarts through the watchdog. In a RUN-pin or brownout reset the pads return to their reset state: output high impedance, input disabled, pulled low at 36 to 113 kOhm (section 9.3; Table 1436). A 244's inputs then read low: +-5 uA through 113 kOhm is 0.57 V, under V_IL 0.8 V, so it drives low; the switch passes the pad's low; the 10 kOhm pull-down holds the line; the expander resets with the RP2354B and the control resistors select the pull-down. Through a watchdog reset the pads return to the same state when the watchdog's reset reaches RESETS: pico-sdk's _watchdog_enable sets PSM_WDSEL for every stage except ROSC and XOSC (section 12.9.6.1, lines 52-53); PSM WDSEL bit 4 is RESETS (Table 532); RESETS resets with PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) held (reset value 0x1, Table 535); a PADS reset returns each non-isolated pad to its reset state (section 9.7). Firmware that leaves RESETS out of PSM_WDSEL leaves the pads at their pre-reset level. Not established: whether POWMAN_WDSEL.RESET_SWCORE (Table 490, reset 0x0, not set by the SDK) latches the pre-reset pad state through isolation

found_values.value: Both faults, continuous: a short to ground, and a short to the port's supply pin at up to 8.7 V (F16). The lead carries signal, ground and rail in one plug (IOBoard.md:531) and nothing in the tree limits the current into a shorted signal line (IOBoard.md:536). Series resistance per gated line, between the gate element and the connector, with the clamp and the bias network on the gate element's side. Lower bounds: a line driven by the RP2354B pad through the switch takes at least 275 Ohm (3.3 V / 12 mA, the highest drive setting Table 1436 characterises); a line driven by a 244 takes at least 142 Ohm (3.4 V / 24 mA, its recommended output current). Upper bound on the multiprotocol and UART lines in servo configuration mode: the servo's open-drain low reaches the pin at V = (3.3/1000 + Vs/R) / (1/1000 + 1/10000 + 1/R), which is 0.70 V + 0.77 Vs at 275 Ohm, so it stays at or under V_IL 0.8 V only while the servo's output-low voltage Vs is 0.13 V or less (0.074 V at 300 Ohm). No source read states that voltage, so no value is shown to meet both bounds. A short to 8.7 V puts (8.7 - 3.6) / 275 = 18.5 mA into a 3.6 V clamp and 95 mW into the resistor. The resistor and the clamp are round 2 parts (Research.md Scope)

A STOP, then the operator clear of the F11 latch; no separate switch. The ESC pack switch and the buffer enable both follow the enable node alone (Research.md:281); the pack switch closes within 500 ms of the enable rising (V46), and the gate enables at once. With the programming mode bound before the clear, the RP2354B holds the line high with the pull-up selected, so the ESC powers up with its line high. AM32 stays in its bootloader only when the line never reads low at start-up (bootloader/main.c:1097-1138). BLHeli_S's bootloader waits while the line is high (wait_for_low, BLHeliBootLoad.inc:89-91) and times out about 250 ms (BOOT_DELAY, :10) after it goes low. ESCape32 needs the line high for 2 s at start-up. A Hitec D-series servo needs no power cycle: firmware writes its REBOOT register and it accepts serial 1000 ms later

report.value: A programming session switches no supply of its own. The ESC powers up with its line high after a STOP and the operator clear of the F11 latch: the pack switch and the buffer enable follow the enable node (pack switch closed within 500 ms, V46), and the RP2354B holds the line high through the selected 1 kΩ pull-up. AM32 needs the line never low at start-up, BLHeli_S waits while it is high, ESCape32 needs it high for 2 s. A Hitec D-series servo needs no power cycle: a REBOOT register write, then 1000 ms. VESC: no source read asks for a power cycle

report.figure: connector level in RP2354B reset (RUN, brownout)
report.value: Low on all 21 gated lines (16 PWM, 4 multiprotocol, UART socket). Pads at high impedance, pulled low at 36 to 113 kΩ (section 9.3, Table 1436). SN74LVC244A II ±5 µA gives 0.57 V through 113 kΩ, under V_IL 0.8 V, so the 244 drives low; SN74CBTLV3126 passes the pad's low with the 10 kΩ pull-down; the expander resets with the RP2354B and each SN74LVC1G126 OE pull-down gives Z, so the pull-down alone biases the line. The receiver input's SN74LVC1T45 DIR is held low: receive

report.value: Low, as in a RUN reset, when the watchdog's reset reaches RESETS: pico-sdk's _watchdog_enable sets PSM_WDSEL for every stage except ROSC and XOSC (section 12.9.6.1, lines 52-53); PSM WDSEL bit 4 is RESETS (Table 532); RESETS resets holding PADS_BANK0 and IO_BANK0 (Table 535), and a PADS reset returns non-isolated pads to their reset state (section 9.7). Firmware that leaves RESETS out of PSM_WDSEL leaves the pads, and so the connector, at their pre-reset level. Not established: the effect of POWMAN_WDSEL.RESET_SWCORE (Table 490, reset 0x0). The tree enables no watchdog yet (IOBoard.md:221)

report.value: Two SN74CBTLV3126 parts put 8 OE pins on the node, each with a 10 kΩ pull-down: 8 × 0.33 mA = 2.64 mA at 3.3 V; OE II ±1 µA. The SN74LVC1G04 input adds ±5 µA powered, ±10 µA unpowered (Ioff). The four 10 kΩ OE pull-ups of the two 244s load the inverter output, 1.32 mA, not the node

Lower bounds 275 Ω on pad-driven lines (3.3 V / 12 mA) and 142 Ω on 244-driven lines (3.4 V / 24 mA). Upper bound in servo configuration mode not shown: the servo's output-low voltage must be 0.13 V or less at 275 Ω (0.074 V at 300 Ω) and no source states it. A short to 8.7 V: 18.5 mA into a 3.6 V clamp, 95 mW in 275 Ω. Round 2 selects the resistor and the clamp

VI −0.5 to 4.6 V absolute maximum (5.1); rail-to-rail switching (section 1); section 5.3 states no switch I/O range and ron is tabulated at VI 0 and 2.4 V only (5.5). A 3.3 V high passes; 3.6 V from a KISS ESC is inside the absolute maximum and not characterised

Recommended VO is 0 to VCC with no 3-state row (5.3); VO in the high-impedance or power-off state −0.5 to 6.5 V absolute maximum (5.1) and IOZ ±10 µA at VO 0 to 5.5 V (5.5). The Nexperia 74LVC244A states the 3-state output at 0 to 5.5 V in its recommended conditions (Table 5)

Through the switch the RP2354B pad drives the connector: V_OH 2.62 V min and V_OL 0.5 V max at 2, 4, 8 or 12 mA by setting (Table 1436); IIOVDD_MAX 100 mA for all GPIO. With the 1 kΩ pull-up selected the pad sinks 2.8 mA while driving low, which needs the 4 mA setting or higher
